Because the pot and your stack size don't give you the option of doing much else.  Because by shoving first on the flop, you'll get hands with equity to fold or force them to draw on your at the best possible odds for your situation.  Given the action preflop it really doesn't matter if you had AA or TT, they're both only a pair now and will be played the same way in this situation.     Why isn't check/call a valid option on the flop?     Given the read on the table, ie passive, anyone willing to bet into you is likely to have a better hand, when a passive player gets aggressive, you should take note and think real hard about what's going on.  Check/call is also incorrect because as mention above, shove is better, even though they accomplish the same thing ie. getting your stack in.  One keeps you in control and telling the aggressive story you're trying to tell by your preflop raise.      It is preferred to open shove here over check/call pretty much always.  Again, see points above about each.      You are pot committed on the turn, easily.  A lot players, myself included, would say you are pot committed on the flop (before you even bet, hence why I argue for a shove).  You want to give your opponents the worst odds possible in order to maximize your value.     By shoving on the flop, you give yourself the best position to win the most money and to win more often because any opponent is getting the worst odds you can give to see the Turn and sometimes you're going to take the pot right there, which is always a good thing.
